items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: In my homeland, the people living under the mountain had a preference for jade wares.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I can only scarcely remember when those delicate jade pendants first came into fashion in the city. They resembled their coins; rounded, with a hole in the center.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Some were glossy green, others pale white. They would feel warm if kept close to the body.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Perhaps that's why it was worth so much.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I first saw it on the belt of a scholar.

items.speaker: Scholar
items.text: ... keep us safe ... in this place ...

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: What is that ...?
He raises his head from behind his wings and to look down through the leaves.
This is not the first time he has heard a human here.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Another seeker of blessings.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I wonder why they put so much trust in the power of this tree ...

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Perhaps they do this simply for peace of mind. I suppose it doesn't matter.

items.speaker: Citizen
items.text: Good day to you, young master. I've seen you up here a lot of late.

items.speaker: Citizen
items.text: Here to pray for the exam? You have shown good devotion. The tree fairy will surely look after you.

items.speaker: Scholar
items.text: I can only hope to be so blessed.

items.speaker: Scholar
items.text: I come here to pray every day, but I do so just to reassure myself, in case I become too nervous in the exam to remember what I have learned.

items.speaker: Citizen
items.text: You ought to play some music underneath the tree.

items.speaker: Citizen
items.text: People say they hear songs coming down from the tree, but no one has ever seen any bird or man playing it. We figure it's a fairy.

items.speaker: Citizen
items.text: And if you play music to please her, the fairy might give you her blessings.
Getian never expected he'd be the cause of a superstition.
He had just learned a song from the bones. It had been a quiet day, and he was practicing.
Who would have thought it could be so misconstrued?

items.speaker: Scholar
items.text: Wouldn't I be ... swaying the fairy's judgment if I did so?

items.speaker: Scholar
items.text: I should just say my wishes as they are. Then it's the fairy's choice to grant them or not.
They converse for a little longer, until the second voice begins to fade away.
Now the only voice is the one which woke him from his dream.

items.speaker: Scholar
items.text: I wish for the people here to live a life of peace, safe from disaster, and that their hard work will be rewarded with bountiful harvests ...

items.speaker: Scholar
items.text: ... that merchants will be safe on their journeys ...

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: His wishes are all about others.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: How curious ...
He loses himself momentarily in thought before casting another glance down to him.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: That backbone ... He may make a good counselor in the court.
He rarely read other creatures' bones outside of his own people.
Bone reading so often makes one curious; and curiosity in turn could be the cause of many troubles.
Even when he wanted to read another creature's bones, he would inevitably talk himself out of it.
He tries, with some difficulty, to not make this an exception.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Pity he will live a disturbed life. Over-righteousness often comes with misfortune.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: He will die for his beliefs. I cannot help but wonder if it might be a …

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: ... No. It's none of my concern.
Gětiān pulls back his glance from the man and his bones.
But the voice inches closer.

items.speaker: Scholar
items.text: I must set out tomorrow.

items.speaker: Scholar
items.text: Let me see. I don't have anything valuable, actually. I'll just leave this here, as a token of sincerity.

items.speaker: Scholar
items.text: I promise to return with better offerings to show my gratitude, well, if my wishes come true that is ...
As the man approaches the tree, the bird withdraws more deeply into its leaves.
There is a rustling of fabric and grass. Something is put on the ground.

items.speaker: Scholar
items.text: Right. This ... should do it.

items.speaker: Scholar
items.text: Farewell.
Gětiān cannot dare to look until all is quiet again.
Below him now is a jade pendant. The same that had hung on the young man's belt.
The bird ponders for a moment and puts it into the tree's hollow.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Nobody will look inside the tree's hollow. It's safer here.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: And should he come back to look for it, I will find a way to return it to him.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: What is lost must be returned, so one may be spared unwanted troubles.
The thought puts his mind at ease. And he returns to his sleep.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: After the young scholar left, life in the forest became quiet again. I spent many long hours in that tree, napping or just listening to the wind.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: But the scholar never returned.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Perhaps it is just as his bones foretold; and he was taken by death young.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Even if I was wrong, mortal lives are short. The pendant no longer had a master.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Until I met its second owner.

items.speaker: Scholar's Son
items.text: So this is the tree Father mentioned. It's more flourishing than I imagined.

items.speaker: Scholar's Son
items.text: I wouldn't be surprised if there truly was a fairy here.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I hadn't seen many blessing-seekers for some time. It seemed now that people only gathered under the tree to talk and laugh before parting ways.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Humans ...

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Hmm?
Seeing this young man recalls a similar scene.
His bones are strangely similar to those of the young scholar who visited so many years ago.
He foresees that this man too will meet a similar end.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I thought people in the outside world cherished their lives more than anything. How come he would rather die than stand by? It's meaningless.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Risking your life just to say something that might not even be adopted. How reckless! It's not worth it.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Is this necessary?
For him, spending so much time in this tree, well perhaps it's merely habit ... But this is where the humans come to make their wishes.
And he listens to their requests, trying to understand what draws his race to them.
He no longer blames his people for leaving home behind. Still, he is puzzled.
... Why did you go into the human world? Why did you sacrifice yourself?

items.speaker: Scholar's Son
items.text: Father, the places you used to talk about, I visited them all.

items.speaker: Scholar's Son
items.text: You warned me not to follow in your footsteps. But I chose this path on my own.

items.speaker: Scholar's Son
items.text: Besides, I have already seen the beauty of the world. I can't bear to watch it being ruined.
Gětiān listens silently from the treetop.
This had been the moment to return the pendant.

items.speaker: Scholar's Son
items.text: Such a beautiful tree should stay here alone, so it won't be destroyed.

items.speaker: Scholar's Son
items.text: Enough empty words. I've made up my mind.
The young man walks away with determination. Never looking back.
The bird knows at that moment he will never see him again.
From then on, he found himself returning to the hollow to check on the pendant.
Within a few short days his prediction appears to come true.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: As I thought.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: What could he have gained from this desperate course of action?
The jade, now broken, seems like little more than a mound of pebbles. But the bird picks them up.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I tried to repair it. Doing the best I could, afterward I tied it to the end of my bone flute.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I thought maybe I would come to understand them more by repairing the jade.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: They struggled for what they knew was impossible, and even died for it unknowingly, just like my people.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Not long after that, a strange rumor went around the village—that people there were being mysteriously turned into horses.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I decided to find out what really happened.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Turns out I am also part of the story.
